summary: Anne MacDonald works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Aklujkar, Geshe Tashi Namgyal, Karin Preisendanz, and Lambert Schmithausen, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Anne Nishimura Morse is a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Harvard under John M. Rosenfield and Yutaka Hirata, and held posts at Smith College, Tokyo National Research Institute, Nara National Museum, and Kyoto National Museum.
Anne Ruth Hansen is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Charles Hallisey and held an attested post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee in 2007.

Annemarie Schimmel was a religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1939–1941). She held posts at Marburg, Ankara, Bonn, and served as professor at Harvard (~1967–1992).
Annette Baier was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago (~1948–1953). She taught Jay L. Garfield and held an attested post at the University of Pittsburgh in 2008.

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) and the University of Vienna (doctoral degree, 2002), studying under David Seyfort Ruegg and Christian Lindtner.

Annette Schmiedchen is an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1985–1990) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1990–1993), later holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~2003–2013) and Humboldt University (~2014).

Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of sinology and religious studies. Educated at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (~1963–1969), he held a post at the University of Chicago from ~1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (~2001–2007) and became Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 2012.

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a sinologist and historian. He studied under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak at Leiden University (~1928–1952), where he later held posts in 1947, 1956–1975, and as professor in 1985.

Anthony Kennedy Warder was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at SOAS under John Brough (~1949–1954). He held posts at the University of Edinburgh (~1955–1963) and the University of Toronto (~1964–1990).

Anthony Tribe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Steven Collins, and earned his DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at Montana and Arizona.
Antoine Lutz specializes in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the supervision of Francisco Varela.

Antoine Meillet was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian/Central Asian specialist who studied at the University of Paris. He held posts at EPHE (~1891–1936), ENLOV (1902–1906), Collège de France (1906–1936), and the Revue des Études Arméniennes.

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist, historian, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He held posts at École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (1795–1838), the Collège de France (1806–1838), and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

Antoine-Léonard de Chézy was an Indologist who studied under Louis-Mathieu Langlès and Silvestre de Sacy. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1799–1832), INALCO, and served as professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1815–1832).
Anton Boller was an Indologist and linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna beginning in 1845, becoming a professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit there in 1855.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1828–1831) and later served there as a Privatdozent in oriental languages in 1849.

Anton Schiefner was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied law at Saint Petersburg State University (~1836–1840) and served as a librarian at the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1852–1879).
Anton Westermann was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University (~1825–1828) and later held a post there from ~1834 to 1869.
